tier_reason: Node PR 61456 states '25% faster for cold importing cjs files' and quotes a Benchmark CI compare run with esm/import-cjs.js cold +26.83 % (+/-0.58 %, ***) and warm +11.95 % (+/-0.14 %, ***); the benchmark code (nodejs/node benchmark/esm/import-cjs.js) is public but the run was launched by merve's own author and no CPU, compiler or flags are given, so first-party with partial methodology (C).

corrections.claimed_speedup: Node PR 61456 body: 'the new cjs module lexer is 25% faster for cold importing cjs files'. Benchmark CI compare run quoted in the PR: esm/import-cjs.js type='cold' +26.83 % (accuracy +/-0.58 %, ***), type='warm' +11.95 % (+/-0.14 %, ***). Node's compare tool reports improvement in operations per second, so +26.83 % corresponds to about 21 % less time per cold import (derived from page data).
corrections.caveats: The numbers come from the PR author's own Node Benchmark CI run (the author, anonrig, also wrote merve); the PR page gives no CPU, compiler or flags and links only to the CI console. The benchmark (nodejs/node benchmark/esm/import-cjs.js) is end-to-end import() of the 2000+-export typescript.js fixture, which includes reading, wrapping and compiling the file, so the lexer-only speedup is not isolated; it compares whole Node builds that also changed the binding (native C++ instead of JS calling wasm), and the cold row includes wasm initialization for the baseline (the warm path's own comment says 'Initialize the wasm first'). The warm row asserts that the imported export names match require(), so it checks correctness. Other rows of the same run are noise-level (esm/detect-esm-syntax +1.47 % and +0.64 %) or noisy (esm-loader-defaultResolve node:os -8.43 % +/-9.28 %). The merve README gives no numbers; its CMakeLists.txt has a MERVE_BENCHMARKS option (default OFF) that calls add_subdirectory(benchmarks), but no benchmarks directory exists in the repository (raw path 404), so the option cannot build. Post-merge correctness regressions: nodejs/node issue 62212 (SIGSEGV when import() analyses a large CJS webpack bundle, bisected to PR 61456, fixed by nodejs/merve PR 41), issue 63323 (FATAL ERROR v8::ToLocalChecked Empty MaybeLocal in cjs_lexer::Parse since v24.14.0, fixed by nodejs/node PR 63885, closed 2026-06-15) and nodejs/merve issue 49 (still open: import * namespace objects lose exports whose names begin with 'get', reported with @tonaljs/chord). The measured build therefore predates several correctness fixes.

notes: Record is accurate; tier C stands (first-party CI run, no hardware or flags, end-to-end import timing that bundles a binding change and wasm start-up). Shortcomings: lexer speed not isolated, benchmark directory referenced by CMake is missing, three post-merge crash or wrong-export regressions (two fixed, merve issue 49 open). Metadata checked: Apache-2.0 OR MIT, 63 stars, not archived or a fork, last commit 2026-04-17 (active).

tier_reason: The ripgrep 0.8.0 README (a widely cited third-party suite, run by a competitor's author) shows ucg 0.163s against GNU grep 0.611s on the Linux kernel [A-Z]+_SUSPEND whitelist search on an Intel i7-6900K; the harness (benchsuite/benchsuite) is public but optimization flags for ucg and grep are not stated, so independent but short of A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: ripgrep 0.8.0 README, Linux kernel tree, whitelist search for whole-word [A-Z]+_SUSPEND: ucg 0.163s vs GNU grep (egrep -R) 0.611s, about 3.7x faster (derived from page data); ripgrep 0.079s, so ucg is about 2x slower than ripgrep. ucg returned 390 lines against 404 for grep and ripgrep. The same suite's 2018-01-08 run (benchsuite/runs/2018-01-08-archlinux-cheetah/summary) shows mixed single-file results against GNU grep 3.1: ucg faster on subtitles_en_literal (0.386 vs 0.803 s, line mode), subtitles_en_literal_word (0.384 vs 0.788 s), subtitles_en_alternate (1.132 vs 1.828 s) and subtitles_ru_alternate (2.043 vs 7.513 s), but slower on subtitles_en_surrounding_words (3.567 vs 1.070 s), subtitles_en_no_literal (5.394 vs 3.446 s), subtitles_ru_literal (2.418 vs 1.089 s) and subtitles_ru_literal_word (2.404 vs 1.114 s).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated in the README table (only 'ripgrep was compiled with SIMD enabled'); commands: ucg --type=cc -w '[A-Z]+_SUSPEND' versus egrep -R -n --include='*.c' --include='*.h' -w '[A-Z]+_SUSPEND'. The suite's 2018-01-08 run README lists ucg 0.3.3-251-g9b5a3e3 built with g++ 7.2.1 (-std=gnu++1z, SSE4.2 and POPCNT in use, PCRE2 10.30 with JIT), GNU grep 3.1 and ripgrep built with RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=native' and simd-accel avx-accel; optimization flags for ucg and grep are not given, and the [A-Z]+_SUSPEND table is not part of that run's summary, so these versions are only probably the README's.
corrections.caveats: The benchmark was run by the author of the competing tool ripgrep (third party to ucg, but a competitor). The README states the CPU (Intel i7-6900K) and the ripgrep build only; the linked blog post was not reachable. ucg's line count differs because of directory traversal: per gvansickle/ucg issue 106 (opened by BurntSushi, closed 2017-05-07), ucg's multithreaded traversal skips directories already reached through a symlink, so it searched fewer files than egrep -R, which follows symlinks (grep -r without symlink following also returns 390), so ucg did slightly less work in that row. ucg is not uniformly faster than GNU grep: in the same suite's 2018-01-08 single-file subtitles runs it is slower than grep 3.1 on the surrounding-words, no-literal and Russian literal patterns (up to about 3.3x slower) while faster on English literal and alternation patterns. ucg's own README has a first-party table (Boost 1.58.0 source, pattern '#include\s+.*', Fedora 25, average of 10 runs): ucg 0.3.0 0.228973s, ripgrep 0.2.9 0.167586s, ag 0.32.0 2.29074s, GNU grep 2.26 0.370082s (about 1.6x slower than ucg, derived); its 'Num Diff Chars' column shows ucg output differing from grep's by 189 characters (9511 matched lines against 9509); that table is first-party with no CPU or flags, and ripgrep wins it. All numbers are from 2016-2018 versions; ucg is slower than ripgrep in every source. Recent commits (2026-09-14) are CI, m4 and perf-comparison script changes; the last source-code change is from 2024-12-28. ucg's tests/performance_tests.at and tests/benchmark_progs.csv can regenerate a comparison, but no recent numbers are published.

notes: Record accurate; tier B stands (third-party ripgrep suite, CPU stated, flags missing). Main shortcomings: competitor-run benchmark from 2018, ucg searched fewer files than egrep -R in the quoted row (symlink traversal), and the same suite shows ucg slower than GNU grep on several single-file regex patterns; ripgrep beats ucg everywhere. Metadata checked: GPL-3.0-only, 144 stars, 18 forks, not archived or a fork, last commit 2026-09-14 (active).
